Cognate with {{cog|sco|gif||if, whether}}, {{cog|stq|af}}, {{m|stq|of||if, whether}}, {{cog|fy|oft||whether}}, {{cog|nl|of||or, whether, but}}, {{cog|gml|ef}}, {{m|gml|if}}, {{m|gml|af}}, {{m|gml|of}} {{gloss|"if; whether"; > {{cog|nds-de|of}}}}, {{cog|de|ob||if, whether}}, {{cog|is|ef||if}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|ĭf}}, {{IPA|en|/ɪf/}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-if.wav|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-if.wav|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-if.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪf|s=1}} ===Conjunction=== {{en-head|conj}} # [[supposing|Supposing]] that, [[assuming]] that, in the [[circumstance]]s that; {{ng|suppositive used to introduce a [[condition]] that may be (or prove to be) either true or false.}} #: {{ux|en|I'll do it next week '''if''' I have time.}} #: {{ux|en|Fetch me a cold beer '''if''' there's one in the fridge.}} #: {{ux|en|'''If''' I give you the money, will you buy it for me?}} #: {{ux|en|'''If''' you prefer, I can come tomorrow instead.}} ## {{lb|en|computing}} A keyword that invokes conditional processing: in the event that a given condition is true, execute the given statement(s) (otherwise execute other statements). ##: {{ux|en|'''if''' A then B else C}} # Supposing that; {{ng|used with past or past perfect subjunctive to indicate a [[counterfactual]] or [[hypothetical]] condition.}} #: {{ux|en|'''If''' she hadn't told me, I wouldn't know.}} #: {{ux|en|'''If''' he understood how this made me feel [[right now]], he'd be O.K. with it too.}} #: {{ux|en|'''If''' I was King of England, I'd make you my Queen.}} #: {{ux|en|She could have used my car '''if''' the battery hadn't been flat.}} ## {{lb|en|usually|hyperbolic}} [[even|Even]] if; even in the circumstances that. ##: {{ux|en|I wouldn't marry you '''if''' you were the last man on earth.}} ##: {{ux|en|You're finishing your chowder '''if''' you sit there all afternoon!}} ##* {{RQ:Dickens Oliver Twist|text=“Wait a minute!” said the girl: “I wouldn’t hurry by, if it was you that was coming out to be hung, the next time eight o’clock struck, Bill. I’d walk round and round the place till I dropped, '''if''' the snow was on the ground, and I hadn’t a shawl to cover me.”}} ##* '''2004''', {{w|David Lee Murphy}} and Kim Tribble (writers), {{w|Montgomery Gentry}} (singers), “'''If''' It’s The Last Thing I Do” (song), in ''You Do Your Thing'' (album): # Considering the fact that; [[given that]]; {{n-g|introducing a condition that is known to be true}}. #: {{ux|en|The drain's blocked — and '''if''' the drain's blocked, the water won't flow.}} #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|year=1596.1|book=I|stanza=ii|page=66|passage=O what of Gods then boots it to be borne, / '''If''' old ''Aveugles'' ſonnes ſo euill heare?}} # [[when|When]]; [[whenever]]; every time that. #: {{ux|en|'''If''' you heat water to 100° C, it boils.}} #: {{ux|en|'''If''' it rains, it pours.}} # [[although|Although]]; {{ng|used to introduce a concession}}; may..but. #: {{ux|en|He was a great friend, '''if''' a little stingy at the bar.}} #: {{ux|en|She won her team's admiration, '''if''' not the award, for her performance.}} # {{lb|en|literary}} [[while|While]]; {{ng|used to introduce a contrast}}. #: {{ux|en|'''If''' tea is expensive, coffee is completely unaffordable.}} #* {{RQ:Nabokov Pnin|chapter=3.3|page=66|passage='''If''' his Russian was music, his English was murder.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2015|author=Phillips Payson O'Brien|title= How the War was Won: Air-Sea Power and Allied Victory in World War II|page=[https://www.google.com/books/edition/How_the_War_Was_Won/9hh2BgAAQBAJ?&gbpv=1&pg=PA103 103]|passage=If the Americans knew how they wanted to use strategic air power but not what to attack, the British had a huge number of plans about what to attack but almost no means to adequately deliver the necessary blow.}} # {{lb|en|sometimes|_|proscribed}} [[whether|Whether]]; {{ng|used to introduce a noun clause, an indirect question, that functions as the direct object of certain verbs.}} #: ''I don't know '''if''' I want to go or not.'' #* '''1715–1717''', {{w|Matthew Prior}}, ''Alma; or, The Progress of the Mind'', Canto III: #*: Quoth Matthew, “{{...}} / She doubts '''if''' two and two make four, / {{...}}” #* {{quote-book|en|year=1976|author=Michael Harrison|title=Beyond Baker Street: A Sherlockian Anthology|page=117|passage=It is doubtful '''if''' the Victorian Londoner needed any warning, for the artful mobsmen, toolers, whizzers and dippers, together with their stickman accomplices, were everywhere in the crowds, in the underground, on railway trains {{...}}}} # {{ng|Introducing a [[relevance conditional]]}}; in case. #: {{ux|en|I have leftover cake '''if''' you want some.}} #: {{ux|en|'''If''' you want to go home, I have the car keys.}} ====Usage notes==== * Specifically a [[subordinating]] conjunction. * Some usage critics recommend that ''if'' not be used to mean ''whether'', since the distinction can remove ambiguity, as in the following example: :: ''Tell me if you can see her.'' (If the addressee can see her, then they must let the speaker know) :: ''Tell me whether you can see her.'' (The speaker wants to know which instance is true: either the addressee's ''ability'' '''or''' ''inability'' to see her) * This distinction is further encouraged because, traditionally, ''if'' cannot always be used in place of ''whether''. For instance, if the noun clause acts as the subject of the sentence or an object of a preposition, the word is usually ''whether''. Examples: :: ''We like to talk about whether classical music is better than jazz.'' :: ''Whether you like today’s weather does not matter.'' * Another difference between ''if'' and ''whether'' is with the use of ''or not''. :: The sentences ''I don't know whether or not I passed'' or ''I don't know whether I passed or not'' are both correct :: The sentence ''I don't know if I passed or not'' is correct, but ''I don't know if or not I passed'' is incorrect ====Alternative forms==== * {{l|en|eef}} {{q|representing various accents}} * {{l|en|ifen}}, {{l|en|iffen}}, {{l|en|if'n}} {{q|dialectal}}
